transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-28
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~50 min
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Shah (Redwood SE), John Reyes (Ember - SecOps), Lina Park (Ember - CTO), Matt O'Neil (Ember - Cloud)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Alex, AE on the account, Maya and Ravi are gonna walk through our audit logs and admin activity today.
[00:12] John Reyes: Thanks Alex, appreciate it. Our main ask is we need to understand exactly what is captured, options to push logs to our SIEM, retention limits and encryption. Also Lina's here to confirm compliance needs.
[00:25] Lina Park: Hi team. We have regulatory requirements for retention in EU region and want proof of immutability for certain admin events.
[00:34] Maya Patel: Great, we'll cover what events are logged, export routes - S3, webhook, syslog/rsyslog to SIEM, live streaming options - and retention configuration. Quick note: transcription may be a bit raw, sorry if I stutter.
[00:48] Ravi Shah: I'll start with schema at high level. Each audit event has fields: timestamp, actor (user/email or service identity), action (create/update/delete/login, token_create), target resource (route/model_id/config_id), request_id, ip, user_agent, org_id, before/after snapshot for admin changes, and outcome (success/fail).
[01:10] Matt O'Neil: Do you capture role changes and SSO group mappings?
[01:14] Maya Patel: Yes - role grants/revokes, SSO assertions, SAML/OIDC login events, and group syncs are recorded. For SSO we log identity provider, nameid, assertion timestamp, but note we don't persist full raw assertion by default - it's metadata.
[01:30] John Reyes: How granular is the before/after? Like if an admin flips a setting in the Console, is the exact param shown?
[01:36] Maya Patel: We capture diffs for config changes with key/value before/after. For sensitive fields (passwords, secrets) we redact values and store a placeholder like "[REDACTED]" and a hash so you can verify a change occurred.
[01:52] Lina Park: And retention - what's default and what can we configure for Dedicated or Private deployments?
[01:58] Ravi Shah: Hosted (Redwood API) default retention is 90 days for audit logs. For Dedicated we can extend to 1 year or custom SLAs as part of reserved capacity. For Private (VPC/on-prem) you control retention entirely - logs can be pushed to your S3 or on-prem ELK with no Redwood retention if you choose.
[02:18] Alex Chen: Also we offer longer term archival options: we can export daily batches to a customer-owned S3 bucket with lifecycle, or stream events in near real-time to your SIEM via syslog or Kafka connector.
[02:30] John Reyes: If we export to S3, is the export encrypted with our KMS?
[02:34] Maya Patel: Yes - server-side encryption to your S3 with customer-managed KMS keys is supported. For logs stored in Redwood-managed storage we encrypt at rest using our KMS; for Private we can integrate with your HSM or KMS. We'll send you the KMS integration guide.
[02:52] Matt O'Neil: What about tamper-evidence / immutability - can we set WORM on exported logs?
[02:57] Ravi Shah: On exports to your S3, you can enable S3 Object Lock/WORM. Within our managed system we maintain append-only write semantics and write-audit ids, and we can provide signed log digests on request for certain entitlements - we'll follow up on scope.
[03:14] Lina Park: Do you capture access to embeddings or model outputs? Particularly if someone queries PII, do you log input/output?
[03:21] Maya Patel: We log request metadata and request_id along with model ID and route. By default full request/response bodies are not stored long-term in hosted mode to avoid PII retention; we store a hashed pointer and metadata. Customers on Dedicated/Private can opt into storing full payloads for debugging/qa, but must attest to handling PII. We also have configurable redaction rules on the ingestion side.
[03:45] John Reyes: Is there a way to stream logs to our SIEM with guaranteed ordering / no loss?
[03:51] Ravi Shah: Real-time streaming is at-least-once; we include request_id and sequence numbers per shard to help ordering. For strict exactly-once you should rely on S3 batch exports with checksums; streaming plus downstream dedupe is the common pattern.
[04:07] Alex Chen: Quick interjection - some words might sound off in the transcript, but main point: we provide both near-real-time and batched exports.
[04:15] Matt O'Neil: What about query capabilities - can we search logs in Redwood Console?
[04:19] Maya Patel: Yes, the Console has a log explorer with filters by actor, action, request_id, IP, timeframe. Role based access controls (RBAC) limit who can view logs; audit_viewer role can see events but not payloads unless granted.
[04:35] John Reyes: RBAC mapping to SSO - can we map our AD groups to Redwood roles?
[04:40] Ravi Shah: Absolutely, we support SAML group mapping and SCIM for provisioning. You can map AD groups to Redwood roles (admin, audit_viewer, dev, ops).
[04:50] Lina Park: We need export logs to EU region and ensure data residency. How is that enforced?
[04:56] Maya Patel: We can configure regional storage: logs generated in EU-region clusters are stored in EU storage; exports to your customer S3 can be configured to a region of your choice. For Hosted customers, we provide a regional tenancy option on enterprise plans.
[05:10] John Reyes: Any PII masking help? e.g. mask account numbers in request bodies?
[05:14] Maya Patel: We have configurable ingestion rules to redact fields (regex or JSON path). We can apply masking on the server side before persistence or on export. For Private, you can bring your own masking pipeline.
[05:27] Matt O'Neil: Do you provide schema examples? We want to validate mapping into our SIEM.
[05:31] Maya Patel: Yes - I'll share a JSON schema and a CSV sample. The fields include event_type, timestamp, actor_id, actor_email, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, ip, user_agent, region, outcome, diff_before, diff_after (diffs are JSON strings).
[05:53] John Reyes: How big are logs? Rough order of magnitude for our volume estimate: we do ~200k inference requests/day and 40 admin actions.
[06:02] Ravi Shah: Inference request metadata is small - say 1KB per event if you log metadata only; if you store full payloads add 200-500 bytes or more based on prompt size. So estimate 200k * 1KB = ~200MB/day. Admin actions are negligible.
[06:18] Alex Chen: Note pricing for long-term storage depends on retention and export frequency - we'll include a rough cost model in the follow-up.
[06:26] Lina Park: Auditing and alerts - can we get alerts for suspicious admin behavior?
[06:30] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood Console supports alerts on patterns (failed logins, mass role changes, unusual IPs). Alerts can create tickets, send webhooks, or integrate with PagerDuty.
[06:41] John Reyes: For compliance, we need a chain of custody / proof of who initiated a change - do you capture session IDs and MFA factors?
[06:48] Ravi Shah: We capture session IDs and SSO auth methods (SAML assertion details). MFA challenge success/failure events are logged. The event includes actor, auth_method, mfa_result. That should satisfy chain of custody in most audits.
[07:01] Alex Chen: Question from the backlog - can we restrict who can export logs?
[07:04] Maya Patel: Yes, export permission is gated by role. Only people with export_data and audit_admin roles can perform exports, and exports are logged as events themselves.
[07:14] Matt O'Neil: Do you support signed exports for integrity verification?
[07:18] Ravi Shah: We can provide signed SHA256 digests for export batches and an audit manifest. For higher assurance we can work on a signed timestamp service as an add-on.
[07:30] Lina Park: Are there SOC2 controls around logs retained in Redwood-managed storage?
[07:35] Alex Chen: Yes - Redwood SOC2 Type II covers logging, change management, encryption, and access controls. We'll attach the Type II report and a mapping to your control framework.
[07:45] John Reyes: Can we see sample logs for sensitive scenarios? e.g. an admin deleted a model and rolled back?
[07:52] Maya Patel: We'll include a sample showing delete model event with before/after, request_id and user info - with PII scrubbed.
[07:59] Matt O'Neil: How do you handle retention requests from users (right to be forgotten)?
[08:04] Ravi Shah: For hosted customers, we have data deletion APIs and redaction flows; logs that are part of an audit trail may be retained according to retention policy but we can discuss targeted deletion for PII fields. For Private, it's your process.
[08:20] Alex Chen: Quick pause - any other blockers?
[08:23] John Reyes: One more: export latency - if we trigger a bulk export, how long until files appear in our S3?
[08:28] Maya Patel: For daily batch exports it's typically within 15-30 minutes after the end of the window. Near-real-time streaming to Kafka or syslog is sub-second to seconds depending on network.
[08:39] Lina Park: Can you enforce encryption in transit to our SIEM endpoint?
[08:43] Ravi Shah: Yes, we support TLS for webhooks, syslog over TLS, and mTLS for Kafka connections.
[08:51] John Reyes: Any limits on export throughput? We might need a high ingest peak when replaying logs.
[08:56] Maya Patel: There are throughput quotas per account; for Dedicated we can size capacity and guarantee throughput. For hosted customers we throttle to protect stability, but support burst patterns to an extent. We'll include recommended throughput and a sizing guide.
[09:10] Alex Chen: That covers the bulk. Let's quickly recap next steps.
[09:13] Maya Patel: I'll share the JSON schema + CSV sample, a sample export with PII scrubbed, and KMS integration doc.
[09:20] John Reyes: I'll confirm retention window and region and reply.
[09:24] Lina Park: We'll schedule the SIEM deep dive for the week of Jan 11.
[09:28] Alex Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the SOC2 and the sample exports.
[09:34] System (automated): Meeting ended at 15:50 PST

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions, product names sometimes garbled (e.g. "K-V cache"), speaker labels approximated.
